case_content.title: Prompt #1 - Airline Expansion
case_content.content: A major airline is considering acquiring an existing route from Tokyo to New York. How can it determine if the route is a good idea?

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Framework
case_content.content:
Suggested frameworks:

Profitability analysis looks like the best approach. Simply determine if revenue less costs equals a positive profit. Then, analyze the factors that go into revenue and the factors that comprise cost to come to a conclusion.

case_content.title: Expected Analysis - Fact Gathering
case_content.content:
Interviewer Notes:

Revenues will be determined by occupancy rates and expected prices. Both of these will be determined by expected demand, the competitive environment and the extent to which our client could win over passengers from competitor routes.

Operating costs will depend on expected fuel costs, incremental costs for landing rights, etc. It is also very important to estimate the cost of cannibalization on existing Tokyo-LA, LA-New York routes. And, last but not least, it is important to note that losing passengers to cannibalization is better than losing them to competitors.

case_content.title: Key Findings
case_content.content:
The attractiveness of the route should be determined through a profitability analysis. The airline should estimate whether expected revenues from the Tokyo-New York route exceed the incremental costs of operating or acquiring the route.

Revenue depends on expected occupancy rates and ticket prices, which are driven by market demand, competitive dynamics, and the client’s ability to win passengers from competitor routes. Costs include operating costs such as fuel and landing rights, as well as the impact of cannibalization from the airline’s existing Tokyo-LA and LA-New York routes.

Cannibalization should be considered carefully, but losing passengers to the airline’s own new route may be preferable to losing them to competitors.

case_content.title: Final Recommendation
case_content.content: Based on your analysis, what recommendation would you give the client?

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Final Recommendation
case_content.content: A strong candidate should recommend acquiring the route only if expected incremental revenue exceeds incremental operating costs and the net effect of cannibalization. The candidate should consider occupancy rates, pricing, demand, competitive environment, ability to win passengers from competitor routes, fuel costs, landing rights, and cannibalization of existing Tokyo-LA and LA-New York routes. The candidate should also recognize that cannibalizing the airline’s own passengers may be strategically better than losing those passengers to competitors.
